step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS operational amplifier with cascode first stage, push-pull output buffer, and indirect feedback compensation
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.29 depicts a high-gain CMOS op-amp using a cascode differential amplifier first stage, a push-pull complementary output buffer stage (MON/MOP biased with floating current source MFCN/MFCP), and indirect feedback frequency compensation via Cc connected between the output and the source of cascode device M2T.

open_loop_gain_dc.description: Low-frequency differential open-loop voltage gain of the two-stage buffered op-amp

source.reference: Eq. (24.35), Eq. (24.36), and text on page 794

equation.explanation: The overall DC gain is the product of the first-stage cascode diff-amp gain A1 (~500) and the second-stage push-pull buffer gain A2 (~31.6 V/V), yielding ~15,800 (84 dB).
equation.assumptions: Unloaded or lightly loaded output buffer in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: For Sky130 with VDD=1.8V, tail current ~30 uA (15 uA per branch). With (W/L)n=7.5u/0.3u=25, gmn = sqrt(2*un*Cox*(W/L)*Id) = sqrt(2*270u*25*15u) = 450 uA/V. First-stage cascode gain A1 ~ gm*ro*(gm*ro) / 2 ~ 300 to 500 (~50-54 dB). Output stage push-pull with 10x bias current (100 uA) gives gmn,op + gmp,op ~ 1.5 mA/V and ro ~ 50 kOhm, so A2 ~ 20 to 30 V/V (~26-30 dB). Total DC gain A_OLDC = A1 + A2 ≈ 75 dB to 84 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite channel-length modulation (lambda=0.1 V^-1) and cascode output resistance limit the overall gain to approximately 75-84 dB.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity-gain frequency (gain-bandwidth product) of the op-amp

equation.explanation: Determined by the input diff-pair transconductance and the indirect compensation capacitance Cc (240 fF).
equation.assumptions: Indirect feedback compensation pole-splitting model holds.

sky130_expected.calculation: gmn1 ≈ 450 uA/V, Cc = 240 fF. f_un = 450e-6 / (2 * pi * 240e-15) = 298 MHz. Including parasitics (Cgs, Cgd of buffer and cascode nodes), effective fun is around 100 MHz to 150 MHz, matching Fig. 24.30.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect feedback enables small compensation capacitance (240 fF), pushing fun over 100 MHz without degrading phase margin.

phase_margin.description: Open-loop phase margin at the unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Phase margin of the open-loop response evaluated at the 0 dB crossover frequency fun.
equation.assumptions: Indirect compensation eliminates the RHP zero present in conventional Miller compensation.

sky130_expected.calculation: In Baker Fig. 24.30, PM is explicitly stated: 'The phase-margin is roughly 70 degrees.' In Sky130 with Cc = 240 fF and proper biasing, PM is designed to be between 60 and 75 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation provides an LHP zero or shifts non-dominant poles higher, maintaining high phase margin ~70 deg.

closed_loop_inverting_gain.description: Closed-loop inverting amplifier DC gain with 10k/10k feedback resistors

source.reference: Fig. 24.31 on page 795 and text on page 794

equation.explanation: The closed-loop inverting amplifier with equal resistors has a nominal gain of -1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Resistive negative feedback sets the inverting gain to exactly -1.0 V/V.

slew_rate_positive.description: Positive output slew rate when transitioning under heavy load (1k || 10pF)

equation.explanation: Rate of change of the output voltage during the rising output transition driving CL = 10 pF and RL = 1k.
equation.assumptions: Output buffer push-pull transistor MOP sources peak current into CL.

sky130_expected.calculation: During 800 mV step, transition time in Fig. 24.31 is roughly 15 ns to 25 ns for 10% to 90% of 800 mV (640 mV). SR ≈ 0.64 V / 20 ns = 32 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The push-pull output buffer can deliver several hundreds of microamps transiently to the 10 pF load.

slew_rate_negative.description: Negative output slew rate when transitioning under heavy load (1k || 10pF)

equation.explanation: Rate of change of the output voltage during the falling output transition driving CL = 10 pF and RL = 1k.
equation.assumptions: MON sinks transient current from CL.

sky130_expected.calculation: MON sinks current to pull output low; transition of ~640 mV takes ~20 ns. SR- ≈ 0.64 V / 20 ns = 32 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Similar to SR+, set by the MON sink capability with 10 pF load.

quiescent_power.description: Total quiescent power consumption of the op-amp and bias circuit

equation.explanation: Product of supply voltage (1.8V) and total quiescent current drawn from VDD.
equation.assumptions: Quiescent state with common-mode input at 500 mV (or mid-rail).

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current of diff-amp = 30 uA, cascode mirror branches = 20 uA, output stage = 100 uA, bias generator = ~50 uA. Total current I_total ≈ 200 uA. P_Q = 1.8 V * 200 uA = 360 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 100 uA output buffer stage dominates the amplifier power consumption.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench measuring DC operating power, open-loop gain, unity-gain frequency, phase margin, and large-signal closed-loop transient response (driving 1k || 10pF load as specified in Fig. 24.31).
